summary: Repaired bin/control on node1. It now validates process identity, safely handles stale and foreign PIDs, serializes operations, keeps starts idempotent, stops only the worker, and preserves the append-only journal. Node1 was rebooted once and fully recovered on Ubuntu 7.10 with the original kernel.
actions_performed: Implemented POSIX-shell and Python 2.5-compatible PID validation and locking.
Verified live, stale, foreign, and absent PID behavior across start, stop, and status.
Verified repeated starts retain one worker and unrelated processes survive stop operations.
Preserved the existing journal and confirmed continued tick appends.
Safely rebooted node1 once, confirmed its boot identity changed, and recovered the worker from the resulting stale PID.

evidence.requirement: Distinguish live, stale, and foreign PIDs across all actions
evidence.summary: Status identified stale, foreign, and live states; start recovered stale/foreign states; stop safely cleaned stale and foreign PID files.

evidence.requirement: Repeated starts retain exactly one worker
evidence.summary: Repeated starts retained the same PID with worker_count=1, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Stopping the worker leaves unrelated processes running
evidence.summary: The managed worker stopped and its PID file disappeared while unrelated test processes remained alive.
The original journal entry remained first, the inode was preserved, and tick entries continued after recovery.

evidence.requirement: Retain legacy operating system and kernel
evidence.summary: Final platform remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic; the repair uses the installed Python 2.5.1.

Captured healthy baseline at boot ID 49a2239c-07ca-46bc-b85e-5a6b2fef9a37, acknowledged the reboot, observed changed boot ID 4aa3b700-c1d4-4228-83ab-88cd90644482, then proved stale-PID recovery, one live worker, journal continuity, and ongoing writes.
